exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press
exercises.muscle_targeting_notes: The pressing or forward raising path emphasizes the anterior deltoid; the triceps and upper chest may assist.
instructions: Set a stable stance or seat and start with the hands near shoulder level; brace gently and keep the ribs stacked over the pelvis.
Press the load overhead along a comfortable path, keeping wrists stacked and ribs down; lower slowly to the starting position.
Breathe steadily and keep every repetition within a pain-free range.
End the set when control or stable shoulder positioning is lost.
common_mistakes: Using momentum or excessive resistance to complete the lift.
Shrugging unintentionally or letting the ribs flare during arm movement.
Forcing a painful range or lowering the weight without control.
Holding the breath or allowing posture to collapse as fatigue increases.
safety_cautions: Stop for sharp pain, numbness, unusual shortness of breath, or dizziness; do not push through pinching shoulder pain.
Use a range of motion that is comfortable for your shoulder mobility and reduce resistance if you cannot control the lowering phase.
Secure weights, cables, bands, benches, and wall supports before use; use a spotter for challenging overhead barbell work.
People with a current injury or relevant medical condition should follow advice from a qualified clinician.

exercises.name: Prone W-Raise
exercises.muscle_targeting_notes: The outward or externally rotating path emphasizes the posterior deltoid and/or rotator cuff, depending on the movement.
instructions: Set the resistance light enough to move without shrugging; keep the neck relaxed and lead with the upper arm or shoulder blade as appropriate.
Move the arms outward or toward the target path by drawing the shoulder blades gently together; return slowly without arching the back.
Breathe steadily and keep every repetition within a pain-free range.
End the set when control or stable shoulder positioning is lost.
common_mistakes: Using momentum or excessive resistance to complete the lift.
Shrugging unintentionally or letting the ribs flare during arm movement.
Forcing a painful range or lowering the weight without control.
Holding the breath or allowing posture to collapse as fatigue increases.
safety_cautions: Stop for sharp pain, numbness, unusual shortness of breath, or dizziness; do not push through pinching shoulder pain.
Use a range of motion that is comfortable for your shoulder mobility and reduce resistance if you cannot control the lowering phase.
Secure weights, cables, bands, benches, and wall supports before use; use a spotter for challenging overhead barbell work.
People with a current injury or relevant medical condition should follow advice from a qualified clinician.

Raise the arms in the named direction to a comfortable height without swinging or shrugging; lower slowly.
Breathe steadily and keep every repetition within a pain-free range.
End the set when control or stable shoulder positioning is lost.
common_mistakes: Using momentum or excessive resistance to complete the lift.
Shrugging unintentionally or letting the ribs flare during arm movement.
Forcing a painful range or lowering the weight without control.
Holding the breath or allowing posture to collapse as fatigue increases.
safety_cautions: Stop for sharp pain, numbness, unusual shortness of breath, or dizziness; do not push through pinching shoulder pain.
Use a range of motion that is comfortable for your shoulder mobility and reduce resistance if you cannot control the lowering phase.
Secure weights, cables, bands, benches, and wall supports before use; use a spotter for challenging overhead barbell work.
People with a current injury or relevant medical condition should follow advice from a qualified clinician.
